title: Complexity of the Game of Life limit set
formal: Is the finite-pattern language of the limit set of Conway's Game of Life \(\Pi^0_1\)-complete under total computable many-one reductions? Let \(F:\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z^2}\to\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z^2}\) be the usual B3/S23 update, and set \[\Omega(F)=\bigcap_{n\ge0}F^n(\{0,1\}^{\mathbb Z^2}),\qquad L_\Omega=\{\operatorname{code}(p):[p]\cap\Omega(F)\ne\varnothing\}.\] Here \(p\) is any finite binary pattern on an explicitly specified finite domain. Membership in \(\Pi^0_1\) is known; the question is whether the matching completeness bound holds for this fixed cellular automaton.

source_formulation.text: Is the language of the Game of Life limit set complete for the co-computably-enumerable sets, attaining the general upper bound for cellular-automaton limit-set languages?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of the question following Theorem 2

why: The limit set records which local observations are compatible with arbitrarily long past histories. Matching the co-computably-enumerable upper bound would make this concrete two-state rule as hard as any universal nonhalting condition under computable reductions. The currently known polynomial-space lower bound leaves a major gap between finite resource complexity and undecidability.
status_note: Explicitly open immediately after Theorem 2 of Salo–Törmä, ICALP 2022: PSPACE-hardness is established and Π1^0-completeness is asked. The exact full-plane finite-pattern limit-set predicate was checked on 16 September 2026. Bounded searches of later primary work located no matching resolution; absence of a found result does not prove present openness.

progress.text: Theorem 2 proves PSPACE-hardness of the finite-pattern language and explicitly asks whether the co-computably-enumerable completeness upper bound is reached.
Theorems 1 and 3 establish nonstabilization of iterated images and nonsoficity of the limit set; these results do not settle the stated completeness question.

The finite-pattern domain, full-plane semantics and exact question following Theorem 2 were checked. Bounded searches of later primary work found no matching resolution; this is not a proof of continuing openness.

importance.reason: A sharply defined computability barrier for a canonical universal cellular automaton, with a published PSPACE lower bound and a substantially stronger co-c.e.-completeness target not settled by ordinary universality.

sentences: The limit set of Conway’s Game of Life contains the configurations that have predecessor histories of every finite length.
The question asks whether recognizing finite patterns occurring in that set is complete for the co-computably-enumerable languages.
The pattern is finite, but its surroundings are arbitrary configurations of the infinite plane and are not required to be blank.
The source proves polynomial-space hardness and nonsoficity, neither of which settles the stronger computability-theoretic completeness target.
A resolution would determine whether this canonical cellular automaton attains the general complexity upper bound for limit-set pattern languages.

definitions: A configuration assigns a bit to each point of the infinite square lattice. For a site \(v\), put \(s_v(x)=\sum_{u\in\{-1,0,1\}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}}x_{v+u}\). Simultaneously at every site, \(F(x)_v=1\) exactly when \(s_v(x)=3\), or when \(x_v=1\) and \(s_v(x)=2\); otherwise it is zero. There is no finite boundary or restriction on the configuration outside a tested pattern. A pattern is a function \(p:D\to\{0,1\}\), where \(D\subset\mathbb Z^2\) is finite, and its cylinder is \([p]=\{x:x|_D=p\}\). Encode a pattern by an explicit list of distinct coordinate pairs and their bits, with signed binary coordinates and unambiguous delimiters; malformed strings are rejected. The empty pattern is allowed. Equivalent effective finite-list encodings have the same computable many-one degree. The limit set consists of complete configurations with predecessors of every finite depth, equivalently complete configurations lying in every iterated image; it is not the union of forward orbits of finite populations. A language \(B\) is \(\Pi^0_1\), or co-computably enumerable, if \(w\in B\) is equivalent to \(\forall n\in\mathbb N\ R(w,n)\) for some total decidable predicate \(R\). A many-one reduction from \(B\) to \(L_\Omega\) is one total computable function \(h\) on binary strings with \(w\in B\iff h(w)\in L_\Omega\). Completeness requires such a reduction for every \(\Pi^0_1\) language. There is no polynomial-time restriction on this computability-theoretic reduction, no probability of error and no approximate membership convention. Life itself is fixed; its rule table is not part of the input.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of \(\Pi^0_1\)-completeness for exactly \(L_\Omega\). A positive proof must verify the known membership bound and the required computable many-one hardness. A negative proof must show failure of completeness; merely improving the known lower bound or failing to find a reduction does not suffice. Claims about one-step predecessors, finite-support configurations, forward-time reachability or a modified Life rule settle different languages. The alphabet, infinite lattice, arbitrary surrounding cells and exact limit-set semantics must remain as defined.

context_blocks.text: A finite pattern can occur after one step, after a million steps, or after every possible finite number of steps. The last condition is the one relevant here. Compactness of the full configuration space ensures that a pattern compatible with every iterated image occurs in the intersection defining the limit set.

For a fixed depth, existence of a predecessor for a finite pattern is a finite, decidable constraint problem: the rule has finite propagation speed, so only a finite neighborhood of the pattern can matter. Consequently failure to belong to the limit-set language has a finite-depth witness. This explains the co-computably-enumerable upper bound without assuming that the infinite surrounding configuration is blank.

Theorem 2 of the source proves PSPACE-hardness and immediately asks whether the full computability-theoretic upper bound is attained. PSPACE-hardness alone is compatible with decidability and therefore does not prove the requested completeness. The question preserved here is this explicit bound, rather than an unspecified request to classify every aspect of Life.

The same paper proves that the limit set is not sofic, meaning that it cannot be obtained by projecting all valid tilings of one finite set of local tile rules. This is a structural theorem about symbolic dynamics, not a proof that the finite-pattern language is co-computably-enumerable complete.

Ordinary simulations in Life often rely on carefully arranged surroundings. A pattern-membership statement quantifies existentially over arbitrary surroundings, and those cells may interfere with the intended computation. The paper’s self-enforcing regions control such interference for its lower-bound theorem; ordinary computational universality alone does not close the remaining gap.

Finite-support predecessor questions, periodic-input predecessor questions and forward reachability test different objects. The active target uses finite observations but permits arbitrary infinite configurations and arbitrarily long predecessor histories. The later-work search was limited to matching this predicate; no independently verified resolution was located.
